serving.launch: inkling/serve.sh, MEM=0.75 since 2026-11-21 16:25 Europe/Warsaw (KV ~1.08M tokens per node)
serving.adapter: inkling/shim.py (vLLM dialect; client disconnects close the upstream stream and count as shim:client_cancels)

parts.coding: generic protocol judge (task statement + candidate program, domain-free system prompt, JSON verdict) on every recorded winner of the finished coding arms (715; 31 fail the hidden tests)
parts.arith: second independent call of the unchanged arithmetic judge on every accepted forced plan (49) + equal seeded control of accepted self-closed plans (49) + every rejected forced plan (2,451, --include-rejected-forced)

question: Generic wrong-answer avoidance (owner rule: generic only; Fable round 4 ideas 3 and 4): would a judge acting as a second acceptance key catch wrong coding winners (public tests pass, hidden fail), and would a second judge on forced arithmetic answers change outcomes, at what cost?
decision_rule: Screen only (recorded candidates). A live study of the coding judge as a second key is planned only if it rejects at least half of the wrong winners while rejecting at most 5 % of the correct winners; a live second judge on forced answers only if it would turn at least 1 false accept into a reject per 1,000 forced plans without rejecting more than 1 % of valid accepted plans. Cost reported.
